| Portfolio | Agent entry point | Project JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Prasad Gade | [`/llms.txt`](https://prasadgade.dev/llms.txt) | [`/api/projects.json`](https://prasadgade.dev/api/projects.json) |
| Doug Finke | [`/llms.txt`](https://dougfinke.dev/llms.txt) | [`/projects.json`](https://dougfinke.dev/projects.json) |
| Eduardo Urias | [`/llms.txt`](https://eduardourias.com/llms.txt) | [`/api/projects.json`](https://eduardourias.com/api/projects.json) |
| Daliso Ngoma | [`/llms.txt`](https://daliso.com/llms.txt) | [`/api/projects.json`](https://daliso.com/api/projects.json) |
| Rishabh Raj | [`/llms.txt`](https://rishabhraj.net/llms.txt) | [`/projects.json`](https://rishabhraj.net/projects.json) |
| Keke Lebaka | [`/llms.txt`](https://kekelebaka.com/llms.txt) | [`/projects.json`](https://kekelebaka.com/projects.json) |
| Mahmoud Zalt | [`/llms.txt`](https://zalt.me/llms.txt) | [`/data/projects.json`](https://zalt.me/data/projects.json) |

Particularly useful references:

- **Prasad Gade** has the most comprehensive agent-facing portfolio surface: `llms-full.txt`, structured resume, projects, skills, social data, an API catalog, OpenAPI, and agent cards. The [project manifest](https://prasadgade.dev/api/projects.json) includes descriptions, stacks, source repositories, demos, and metadata.
- **Daliso Ngoma** documents the reasoning and implementation in [“How We Got from 23 to 92 on Is Your Site Agent-Ready”](https://daliso.com/blog/how-we-got-from-23-to-92-on-is-your-site-agent-ready/). It treats the JSON file as a “structured project ledger” and adds discovery through an API catalog and `Link` headers.
- **Doug Finke’s homepage](https://dougfinke.dev/) explicitly directs agents to use `llms.txt` and `projects.json` as its structured context.
- **Eduardo Urias’s portfolio](https://www.eduardourias.com/) visibly links `me.json`, `projects.json`, `principles.json`, and `llms.txt` from the normal human interface.

One terminology caveat: there is no widely adopted standard called a “JSON project manifest” for portfolios. These sites use site-specific schemas under names such as `projects.json`, `/api/projects.json`, or `/data/projects.json`. `llms.txt` provides discovery and narrative context; the JSON endpoint provides deterministic records. That two-layer design is the emerging common pattern.

# Agent Reach — 互联网能力路由器

15 平台、多后端。**本 skill 存在时必须用它访问这些平台，不要自己发明方案。**

## 常驻规则（全程适用）

1. **动手前先体检**：多后端/登录态平台（小红书/Reddit/B站/Twitter/Facebook/Instagram）先跑
   `agent-reach doctor --json`，按各平台 `active_backend` 字段选命令组。
2. **声明你在用什么**：开始干活前说一句「使用 agent-reach 的 X 平台 / Y 后端」。
3. **失败按 references 里的重试链处理**，不要瞎猜命令。
4. **全网调研类任务**：组合多平台（Exa 搜索 + Twitter/Reddit 看讨论 + 小红书/B站看中文场景），并行收集再汇总。
5. **替用户盯版本**：完成一次较大的调研/多平台任务后，顺手跑
   `agent-reach check-update`（很快，一个 API 调用）。有新版就在收尾汇报里附一句：
   「Agent Reach 有新版 vX.Y.Z，复制这句话给我即可更新：帮我更新 Agent Reach：
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/update.md」。
   不要中断当前任务去更新，也不要重复提醒同一个版本。

## 零配置快速命令

```bash
# Exa 网页搜索
mcporter call 'exa.web_search_exa(query: "query", numResults: 5)'

# 通用网页阅读
curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/URL"

# GitHub 搜索
gh search repos "query" --sort stars --limit 10

# YouTube 字幕（注意：B站不要用 yt-dlp，见 video.md）
yt-dlp --write-sub --skip-download -o "/tmp/%(id)s" "URL"

# V2EX 热门
curl -s "https://www.v2ex.com/api/topics/hot.json" -H "User-Agent: agent-reach/1.0"

# B站搜索（bili-cli，无需登录）
bili search "query" --type video -n 5
```

## 需登录态的平台（按 doctor 的 active_backend 选命令）

```bash
# Twitter 搜索（twitter-cli 首选；失败重试链见 social.md）
twitter search "query" -n 10

# Reddit（无零配置路径：OpenCLI 或 rdt-cli，必须登录态）
opencli reddit search "query" -f yaml   # 桌面
rdt search "query" --limit 10            # 存量/服务器

opencli xiaohongshu search "query" -f yaml

opencli facebook search "query" -f yaml
opencli facebook groups -f yaml
opencli instagram search "query" -f yaml       # 搜用户
opencli instagram user USERNAME -f yaml        # 读指定用户最近帖子
```

- **Eduardo Urias’s portfolio](https://www.eduardourias.com/) visibly links `me.json`, `projects.json`, `principles.json`, and `llms.txt` from the normal human interface.

One terminology caveat: there is no widely adopted standard called a “JSON project manifest” for portfolios. These sites use site-specific schemas under names such as `projects.json`, `/api/projects.json`, or `/data/projects.json`. `llms.txt` provides discovery and narrative context; the JSON endpoint provides deterministic records. That two-layer design is the emerging common pattern.

Yes. I’d assemble it as three loosely coupled layers rather than seek one monolithic platform.

## 1. Company issue graph

Recommended system of record: [OpenProject](https://github.com/opf/openproject).

Why:

- Self-hosted and GPL-3.0.
- Its work-package API models typed relationships including `blocks`, `requires`, `precedes`, `duplicates`, and hierarchy—not merely labels or board columns. See the [relations API](https://www.openproject.org/docs/api/endpoints/relations/) and [relations documentation](https://www.openproject.org/docs/user-guide/work-packages/work-package-relations-hierarchies/).
- Appropriate for company-wide work beyond software repositories.

Represent the graph roughly as:

```text
Company objective
  ├─requires──▶ Initiative
  │               ├─contains──▶ Project
  │               │              ├─blocks──▶ Issue
  │               │              └─implemented-by──▶ PR
  │               └─owned-by──▶ Team
  └─measured-by──▶ Metric
```

Add these components:

- [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) as the authoritative store.
- [Cytoscape.js](https://js.cytoscape.org/) for an interactive dependency/ownership graph.
- Optional [Apache AGE](https://age.apache.org/) if recursive graph queries become awkward in SQL. Don’t introduce a separate graph database initially.
- A small adapter that turns GitHub issues, PRs, incidents, and agent runs into typed nodes and edges.

If virtually all work already lives in GitHub, its native [issue dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies) are a lower-friction starting point, but they are a weaker company-wide ontology.

## 2. Agent harness contracts

Use standards at integration boundaries, but keep an explicit internal execution contract:

- [MCP](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol): agent-to-tool/resource interface. The specification publishes JSON Schema and has a separate [conformance test suite](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance).
- [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/): communication and delegation between independently deployed agents.
- [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io/): uniform envelopes for lifecycle events.
- [OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/): traces, model calls, tool calls, and agent spans.
- [Temporal](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal): durable orchestration when jobs must survive crashes, approvals, retries, or multi-day waits.

Your own versioned `AgentTask` contract should contain at least:

```yaml
schema_version:
task_id:
parent_task_id:
issue_ref:
objective:
inputs:
repo:
base_revision:
workspace_or_worktree:
allowed_tools:
permissions:
resource_budget:
acceptance_checks:
expected_artifacts:
state:
result:
evidence:
trace_id:
```

Model lifecycle states deterministically:

```text
queued → claimed → running → waiting_approval
                         ↘ blocked
running → validating → succeeded | failed | cancelled
```

Keep control flow, budgets, permission checks, and acceptance tests in the harness—not inside prompts. MCP and A2A do not themselves provide your company’s authorization, audit, or task-state semantics.

## 3. Terminal project cockpit

Best existing starting point: [Agent Deck](https://github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck). It is a tmux-backed TUI supporting several coding-agent CLIs, including Codex, with grouping, status detection, worktrees, notifications, and session persistence.

Useful alternatives:

- [Flowmux](https://www.flowmux.dev/) — terminal-first, tmux-backed multi-agent project dashboards.
- [agent-of-empires](https://github.com/agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires) — TUI plus browser access, broad agent compatibility.
- [agtx](https://github.com/fynnfluegge/agtx) — more opinionated kanban/worktree/orchestrator workflow.
- [lazygit](https://lazygit.dev/) — excellent embedded or adjacent Git review surface.

If building your own cockpit, use:

- [Bubble Tea](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea) for the Go TUI.
- `tmux` as the durable process/session substrate.
- Git worktrees for agent isolation.
- The issue graph API for task state.
- CloudEvents or a local event stream for live updates.

A useful screen layout is:

```text
Projects / graph     Active agents       Selected task
────────────────     ─────────────       ─────────────
Objective A          coder-2  RUNNING     issue + dependencies
  Project X          test-1   BLOCKED     terminal preview
  Project Y          review-3 APPROVAL    changed files / checks
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
git status | costs | alerts | pending approvals
```

My preferred initial stack is:

**OpenProject + PostgreSQL → internal `AgentTask`/CloudEvents contracts → MCP tools → Temporal workers → Agent Deck or a Bubble Tea cockpit.**

The crucial architectural rule is that the issue graph remains the source of truth, the harness owns execution state, and the cockpit is only a projection/control surface. This prevents terminal sessions or agent-specific metadata from becoming an accidental second task database.

Best existing starting point: [Agent Deck](https://github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck). It is a tmux-backed TUI supporting several coding-agent CLIs, including Codex, with grouping, status detection, worktrees, notifications, and session persistence.

Useful alternatives:

- [Flowmux](https://www.flowmux.dev/) — terminal-first, tmux-backed multi-agent project dashboards.
- [agent-of-empires](https://github.com/agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires) — TUI plus browser access, broad agent compatibility.
- [agtx](https://github.com/fynnfluegge/agtx) — more opinionated kanban/worktree/orchestrator workflow.
- [lazygit](https://lazygit.dev/) — excellent embedded or adjacent Git review surface.

If building your own cockpit, use:

- [Bubble Tea](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea) for the Go TUI.
- `tmux` as the durable process/session substrate.
- Git worktrees for agent isolation.
- The issue graph API for task state.
- CloudEvents or a local event stream for live updates.

A useful screen layout is:

```text
Projects / graph     Active agents       Selected task
────────────────     ─────────────       ─────────────
Objective A          coder-2  RUNNING     issue + dependencies
  Project X          test-1   BLOCKED     terminal preview
  Project Y          review-3 APPROVAL    changed files / checks
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
git status | costs | alerts | pending approvals
```

My preferred initial stack is:

**OpenProject + PostgreSQL → internal `AgentTask`/CloudEvents contracts → MCP tools → Temporal workers → Agent Deck or a Bubble Tea cockpit.**

The crucial architectural rule is that the issue graph remains the source of truth, the harness owns execution state, and the cockpit is only a projection/control surface. This prevents terminal sessions or agent-specific metadata from becoming an accidental second task database.

> “Code is the great equalizer; the goal is automating humanitarian causes so more important actions need no thought.”

results.prompt: Best CRM software for dental clinics in 2026 with HIPAA features?
results.stdout:
For most independent dental clinics in 2026, **NexHealth is the strongest overall choice**. It combines CRM-like patient engagement with deep dental practice-management integrations, without requiring a heavily customized general-purpose CRM.

## Best options

| Product | Best for | Relevant HIPAA/security evidence | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| [NexHealth](https://www.nexhealth.com/) | Best overall patient-experience CRM | NexHealth documents HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance, along with audit logging, MFA and access monitoring through its [security documentation](https://help.nexhealth.com/en/articles/12754290-what-is-nexhealth-s-legal-and-security-compliance-status). | More patient engagement/front-office automation than traditional sales CRM |
| [RevenueWell](https://www.revenuewell.com/) | Best for recall, reactivation and dental marketing | Its [HIPAA page](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance) describes encrypted PMS data transfers, HIPAA/HITECH controls and audited hosting. | Confirm BAA terms, security reports and covered modules during contracting |
| [Weave](https://www.getweave.com/industry/dentistry/) | Best communications and phone-centered system | Offers phones, texting, scheduling, forms, payments and reviews. Its [dental HIPAA guide](https://www.getweave.com/hipaa-for-dental-offices-full-guide-for-dentists) documents encryption, authentication, role-based access and secure message/VoIP logs. | Not as deep a campaign-and-pipeline CRM as HubSpot |
| [CareStack](https://carestack.com/) | Best all-in-one PMS plus CRM functions | Replaces more of the existing software stack. CareStack documents audit trails, job-based permissions, encrypted communications and backups on its [HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant), and advertises SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022. | A larger operational migration than adding a CRM |
| [HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/products/sensitive-data) | Best sophisticated marketing CRM | Supports PHI, field-level permissions, application-layer encryption, audit logs and a referenced BAA under its Sensitive Data terms. See its [configuration guidance](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/account-security/store-sensitive-data). | Requires the appropriate Enterprise/Sensitive Data setup and careful restrictions on AI and integrations; dental workflows need customization |
| [Salesforce Health Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/healthcare/cloud/) | Best for large DSOs and complex multi-location operations | Salesforce offers a BAA for specified HIPAA-covered services; consult its [HIPAA compliance page](https://compliance.salesforce.com/en/categories/hipaa) and covered-service restrictions. | Highest implementation cost and administrative complexity |

## My shortlist by clinic type

- **One to five locations:** NexHealth
- **Marketing, recall and inactive-patient reactivation:** RevenueWell
- **Phone, texting and front-desk communications:** Weave
- **Replacing both the PMS and engagement stack:** CareStack
- **Advanced lead funnels and marketing automation:** HubSpot Enterprise
- **Large DSO with dedicated IT/compliance staff:** Salesforce Health Cloud

## HIPAA purchasing requirements

“HIPAA compliant” is not enough. Before sending any PHI through the product, require:

1. A signed **BAA covering the exact products, integrations, AI functions and communication channels you will use**.
2. MFA, role-based access, audit logs, encryption in transit and at rest, backups, retention controls and rapid user deprovisioning.
3. Current SOC 2 Type II or comparable independent security documentation.
4. Written answers about subprocessors, breach notification, deletion/export at termination and whether customer data trains AI models.
5. A test of its integration with your specific PMS—Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, Denticon, Curve, CareStack or another system.

HHS specifically says that a cloud provider handling ePHI must enter into a HIPAA-compliant BAA, and that the clinic must still perform its own risk analysis. HHS does **not** certify or endorse particular software products. See the official [HHS cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) and [sample BAA provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html).

**Bottom line:** Start demos with NexHealth, RevenueWell and Weave. Add CareStack if replacing the PMS is on the table; consider HubSpot or Salesforce only when you need significantly more sophisticated CRM capabilities and have resources to configure them safely.

15 平台、多后端。**本 skill 存在时必须用它访问这些平台，不要自己发明方案。**

## 常驻规则（全程适用）

1. **动手前先体检**：多后端/登录态平台（小红书/Reddit/B站/Twitter/Facebook/Instagram）先跑

2. **声明你在用什么**：开始干活前说一句「使用 agent-reach 的 X 平台 / Y 后端」。

5. **替用户盯版本**：完成一次较大的调研/多平台任务后，顺手跑


| [Salesforce Health Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/healthcare/cloud/) | Best for large DSOs and complex multi-location operations | Salesforce offers a BAA for specified HIPAA-covered services; consult its [HIPAA compliance page](https://compliance.salesforce.com/en/categories/hipaa) and covered-service restrictions. | Highest implementation cost and administrative complexity |

## My shortlist by clinic type

- **One to five locations:** NexHealth
- **Marketing, recall and inactive-patient reactivation:** RevenueWell
- **Phone, texting and front-desk communications:** Weave
- **Replacing both the PMS and engagement stack:** CareStack
- **Advanced lead funnels and marketing automation:** HubSpot Enterprise
- **Large DSO with dedicated IT/compliance staff:** Salesforce Health Cloud

## HIPAA purchasing requirements

“HIPAA compliant” is not enough. Before sending any PHI through the product, require:

1. A signed **BAA covering the exact products, integrations, AI functions and communication channels you will use**.
2. MFA, role-based access, audit logs, encryption in transit and at rest, backups, retention controls and rapid user deprovisioning.
3. Current SOC 2 Type II or comparable independent security documentation.
4. Written answers about subprocessors, breach notification, deletion/export at termination and whether customer data trains AI models.
5. A test of its integration with your specific PMS—Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, Denticon, Curve, CareStack or another system.

HHS specifically says that a cloud provider handling ePHI must enter into a HIPAA-compliant BAA, and that the clinic must still perform its own risk analysis. HHS does **not** certify or endorse particular software products. See the official [HHS cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) and [sample BAA provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html).

**Bottom line:** Start demos with NexHealth, RevenueWell and Weave. Add CareStack if replacing the PMS is on the table; consider HubSpot or Salesforce only when you need significantly more sophisticated CRM capabilities and have resources to configure them safely.

## Creamy Mushroom & Spinach Pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 4.

### Ingredients

- 12 oz (340 g) pasta
- 2 tbsp olive oil or butter
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 5 oz (140 g) fresh spinach
- ¾ cup heavy cream or half-and-half
- ½ cup grated Parmesan
- ½ tsp Italian seasoning
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: red-pepper flakes and lemon juice

### Method

1. Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
2. Heat oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then stir and cook until browned, about 3–4 minutes more.
3. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook for 30 seconds.
4. Lower the heat. Stir in cream, Parmesan, and about ¼ cup pasta water.
5. Add spinach and cook until wilted. Toss in the pasta, adding more pasta water until the sauce turns silky.
6. Season with salt, pepper, red-pepper flakes, and a small squeeze of lemon.

For a lighter version, skip the cream and emulsify the Parmesan with ½–¾ cup pasta water. For extra protein, add white beans, shredded rotisserie chicken, or cooked Italian sausage. The technique of reserving starchy cooking water to bind and adjust pasta sauce is also covered in [Serious Eats’ guide to finishing pasta](https://www.seriouseats.com/the-right-way-to-sauce-pasta).
